articles.summary: Communications Minister Fahmi Fadzil said NACSA remained on an amber alert after the National Cyber Threat Level was raised earlier in the month, while no worrying cyber incident had been confirmed. He said claims of leaked Malaysian data circulating online were still unverified, and monitoring of financial and critical sectors continued.
articles.title: Nacsa on amber alert amid unverified cyberattack claims, says Fahmi

articles.summary: The Health Ministry disclosed on 12 November a breach limited to a supporting file storage and sharing platform at one of its facilities. It says patient treatment and health services continue as normal. Investigation continues, and a third-party tracker also lists an unconfirmed claim against the ministry's domain.
articles.title: Health Ministry reports cyber breach at facility, services unaffected

articles.summary: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim told Parliament on 3 November that Malaysia is considered a potential cyberattack target because of its digital capabilities and its stance on Gaza. He named no attackers or targets. The warning came a day before NACSA raised the national cyber threat level from Low to Medium.
articles.title: Malaysia a potential cyberattack target, Anwar says

articles.summary: Communications Minister Fahmi Fadzil said on 18 November that claims on dark-web platforms about stolen Malaysian data remain unverified and that no large-scale cyberattack causing a data leak has been reported. The statement follows weeks of heightened alerts and unconfirmed hacking claims affecting banks and agencies.
articles.title: No large-scale cyberattack causing Malaysian data leak reported, says Fahmi

articles.summary: The UK Department for Work and Pensions took Universal Credit, PIP applications, pension services and Tell Us Once offline on 27 November after a cyber incident, working with the NCSC. No data loss is evidenced and payments continue. Officials have not confirmed a deliberate attack and gave no restoration date.
articles.title: DWP shuts benefits services after "serious cyber incident"

articles.summary: Intruders discovered during upgrade work reportedly breached the Air Force Cloud One platform, which hosts personnel, maintenance, logistics and command-and-control applications. Migrations were paused, some users lost admin rights and US Cyber Command joined the probe. Attackers, the exploited flaw and any data theft remain unconfirmed.
articles.title: Hackers breach US Air Force Cloud One platform, pausing IT migrations

articles.summary: Ransomware hit the University Hospital of Guadeloupe on the evening of 21 November, encrypting databases and forcing paper records. Surgeries, chemotherapy and radiation therapy were postponed while emergency, dialysis and urgent cardiac care continued. ANSSI is checking a compromised IT supplier as the entry point; no ransom demand was received.
articles.title: Suspected ransomware attack disrupts cancer treatments, surgeries at Guadeloupe hospital

articles.summary: Bell Canada confirmed an AI-agent-driven intruder breached a pre-production environment of its Maximo ordering and provisioning system on 17 November. Business contact details, ticket text and some network-element IP addresses were taken, but no credentials. Bell reports no customer service impact and has not said how many enterprise customers were affected.
articles.title: Bell Canada says "agentic" hacker stole enterprise customer data

articles.summary: The Dewan Rakyat passed the RM510 billion Supply Bill 2027 by voice vote on 26 November, four weeks after the government signed a confidence and supply agreement with 13 opposition and independent MPs. A development expenditure motion of up to RM85 billion also passed. The bill now goes to the Dewan Negara before royal assent.
articles.title: Dewan Rakyat passes Budget 2027 through voice vote

articles.summary: The Election Commission set nomination day for 28 November and polling for 12 December for the 13th Sarawak state election, with early voting on 8 December. Eighty-two seats are contested; GPS won 76 in 2021. The assembly was dissolved effective 26 October, and 517 nomination forms had been sold by 17 November.
articles.title: Sarawak state election: nomination day on 28 Nov, polling on 12 Dec

articles.summary: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission said on 18 November it is conducting an internal investigation into allegations made by businessman Bachar Kiwan, with its chief commissioner ordering a comprehensive probe. The step is an inquiry rather than a charge, and the agency has not disclosed the substance of the claims or any timeline.
articles.title: MACC conducts internal probe into Bachar Kiwan allegations

milestones.label: Dewan Rakyat resumes with seven bills on the order paper

articles.summary: The Finance Ministry tabled the Finance Bill 2026 and the Tax Collection, Administration and Enforcement Measures Bill 2026 for first reading on 16 November. Both are slated for second reading in the current Dewan Rakyat sitting, which resumes on 30 November with a further seven bills on the order paper.
articles.title: Finance Ministry to table two bills on Monday

articles.summary: MPs pressed ministers on a proposed Nutrition law, illegal crypto mining that steals electricity and rural electric-vehicle charging access during the 16 November Dewan Rakyat session. The items signal possible regulatory and enforcement moves but no bill passage was reported that day.
articles.title: Nutrition Bill, electricity theft by crypto miners and EV charging on Dewan Rakyat agenda

response.text: Schedule an XQL query on proxy and endpoint telemetry for new files or unusual child processes under the MiCollab web directory and traffic to the reported attacker infrastructure. Results land in one case for review. Keep it read-only, with isolation left to an analyst decision.

response.prompt: Summarise the MiCollab hosts in this case: version, internet exposure, patch status (fixed in 10.3.0.18) and any web shell or attacker-IP indicators. Rank by risk and give three next actions. Mark assumptions clearly.
response.text: Use the Cortex AI assistant to turn matches into a short patch-and-hunt brief for the SOC lead. The output lists affected hosts, patch status and indicators of compromise.

response.text: Check the XSIAM Vulnerability and Exposure Management emerging-vulnerabilities view first, since it can already show affected assets without custom playbooks. If MiCollab is internet-facing, a WAF or firewall block on the AWV paths is the quickest interim control.

articles.summary: Five Mitel MiCollab AWV flaws, including command injection rated CVSS 10.0 and an authentication bypass, were exploited before Mitel published patches on 16 November. Accenture saw a web shell on 15 November and attacker contact from 9 November. CISA added all five to KEV on 25 November.

response.text: Use a playbook to find Xen Orchestra instances in your CMDB and scans, confirm versions against 6.9.2 and 6.10.1, and ticket those behind no VPN. Analysts get an exposure list. Restrict management access before patching, with approval.

response.text: Placing Xen Orchestra behind a VPN or allow-list removes the unauthenticated attack path more reliably than detection. Use this as the standing control after patching.

articles.summary: CISA added three Danfoss AK-SM 800A flaws to KEV on 25 November: path traversal, input validation allowing commands (CVSS 9.9) and authentication bypass.
